title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government’s response to the 2020 report outlines a plan to strengthen public standards for AI, emphasizing transparency, accountability, and ethical use across all sectors. It commits to working with regulators, industry, and academia to develop clear guidelines and enforceable frameworks that promote public trust in AI systems.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is outlining how it will oversee the use of AI in educational qualifications, aiming to ensure fairness, reliability, and transparency. The guidance is part of a broader government initiative to address the impact of AI on learning, assessment and industry.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This report examines how copyright‑protected works are used to train AI systems and assesses the legal, economic, and social impacts of that practice. It offers guidance on balancing creators’ rights with the benefits of AI development and identifies potential policy and regulatory changes.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The UK government has replied to the House of Lords Select Committee’s AI report, outlining its strategy for ensuring that artificial intelligence is safe, beneficial and aligned with national values. It commits to stronger regulation, increased investment in research, and closer collaboration with industry, academia and international partners to keep the UK at the forefront of AI while protecting society.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document explains the purpose, scope, and responsibilities of a committee that will examine how artificial intelligence fits with public standards. It also includes a set of frequently asked questions to clarify the committee’s mandate, processes, and expected outcomes.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee’s inquiry into the governance of Artificial Intelligence. The submission outlines CSPL’s views and recommendations for how AI should be regulated and overseen.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: This policy explores how artificial intelligence changes the rules for medical products, focusing on safety, effectiveness, and patient protection. It outlines steps to implement the AI White Paper principles to guide manufacturers, regulators, and stakeholders in managing AI‑driven medical devices.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy is a plan that aims to make the defence organization the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential in AI for its size. It focuses on developing advanced AI capabilities to strengthen national security and give the organisation a global leadership edge.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan explains how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport sector to tap into AI opportunities. It also seeks to manage and mitigate the potential risks that AI could bring.

title: Copyright and artificial intelligence: progress report
description: A progress report on the use of copyright works in the development of AI systems, under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act.
summary: This report outlines how copyright-protected works are being used in the training and development of AI systems under Section 137 of the Data (Use and Access) Act. It reviews progress made, highlights current practices, and identifies challenges and recommendations for balancing intellectual property rights with AI innovation.
